resources.string: What Android reports right now, and what to do about anything that is not set up yet.
No: turn on AI Reply in the list of keyboards
Another keyboard is the default now
Not checked yet: copy a message and tap a recipient in the keyboard
The statuses are read again whenever you come back to the app. Android reports the keyboard itself; paste shows as working after the first successful paste on this phone.
AI Reply is not in the list
Open keyboard settings and look under On-screen keyboard or Manage keyboards; the names differ from phone to phone. If AI Reply is still missing, restart the phone.
It appears for every keyboard that did not come with the phone. Tap OK to turn AI Reply on: it sends text only when you tap Reply or Write.
Tap Choose AI Reply, or, while typing, tap the keyboard icon in the navigation bar. On some phones you press and hold the space bar instead.
The copied message does not appear
Copy the text of the message, not a photo or a file. Text another app marked private, such as a password, is never read.
AI Reply replies to the message you copy. This is how Android handles it.
In the chat, press and hold the message and tap Copy.
Tap the message field and switch to AI Reply.
Tap who you are replying to: AI Reply reads the copied text at that moment.
Android lets only the app on screen, or the keyboard in use, read the clipboard. So AI Reply reads it as your keyboard and only when you tap: never in the background.
Text another app marks private, like a password or a bank code, is hidden from other apps. AI Reply does not read it either: copy the message itself.
From Android 12 the phone may briefly say that AI Reply pasted from the clipboard. That is the system confirming your tap.
There is no separate “allow paste” switch on Android: nothing needs to be turned on.
No paste in AI Reply on this phone yet.
Good afternoon! Could you tell me how much delivery to Almaty costs and when you could bring it?
Add a message or try the example
There is no text on the clipboard. Copy the message, then tap Paste.
The copied text is marked private, such as a password, so AI Reply does not paste it. Copy the message itself.
The copied text could not be read. Copy the message again.
Reply to clients with confidence and chat easily with the people close to you. Right from the keyboard.
Hi! It’s been a while. How are you?
Hi! So good to hear from you. Tell me, how have you been?
First copy the message you want to reply to. Try it here.
Good afternoon! Could you tell me more?
In any messenger: press and hold the message, then tap Copy.
Tap who you’re replying to. In the keyboard these buttons sit above the letters.
The choice sets the tone and how formal the reply is: warm for a friend, polite for a client or a partner, plain and to the point for a colleague.
Pick who it’s for and see the reply change. Nothing is sent here and no replies are used.
Hi! Sure, happy to tell you. What would you like to know?
Good afternoon! Of course. Could you tell me what exactly you’re interested in? I’ll explain everything in detail.
Hi! Yes, of course. What exactly should I clarify?
Good afternoon! Certainly. Let’s go over the details: when would be a good time for a call?
This is how AI Reply works in any messenger: the reply appears in the keyboard, and you send it yourself.
A couple of steps in Android settings, and AI Reply is there in every messenger.
Choose AI Reply as the default keyboard

Android shows the same warning for every keyboard that did not come with the phone: it “may be able to collect all the text you type”. AI Reply sends text only when you tap %1$s or %2$s (the copied message and your request) and, with Smart correction on, the request while you type it in AI Reply’s own field. Nothing else you type leaves the phone.
Check it: tap the field, and the AI Reply keyboard should appear.
The AI Reply keyboard is on screen: everything works.
